title: Animation
text: Four verbs, added plot: transition_states(states) — marks column whose levels states. ease_aes(ease) — chooses easing (interpolation accelerates). animate(nframes, fps) — compiles keyframes returns vellum_animation. anim_save(file, animation) — tweens encodes frames file. output format follows file extension: .gif looping animated GIF (universally viewable), .png animated PNG (APNG — lossless, transparency), .svg animated SVG. tween, parallel render across CPU cores, streaming encode happen one pass vellum’s Rust backend. .svg writes single animated SVG: every frame emitted vector markup shown turn CSS step animation. Two things make worth reaching . resolution-independent — file crisp slide, retina screen, print, raster format . honours prefers-reduced-motion: reader asked system animate shown one still frame, extra work – last frame animation ends final state (reveal, transition_time(), non-looping transition_states()), otherwise first. animated SVG namespaces CSS, several can share one HTML page. trade-size. every frame emitted full, animated SVG grows number marks times number frames, GIF . wins clearly line art — handful moving marks, common explanatory case — loses dense scatter, raster format right answer. Choose mark count, preference; anim_save() says .svg scene dense enough raster format likely smaller. Serve gzipped (.svgz, web server compression) shrink several-fold.

text: viral “bar chart race” needs special API — ordinary transition_states() animation long-format data. bar keyed category, tween slides bars past one another ranks change states, frozen scales keep value axis jumping. coord_flip() makes bars horizontal (familiar racing layout); rank categories within year first want sorted top--bottom.
code: #| eval: false set.seed(1) cats <- c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E") race <- do.call(rbind, lapply(2000:2006, function(y)   data.frame(year = y, cat = cats,              value = pmax(1, runif(5, 1, 10) + (y - 2000) * c(2.5, 1, 0.4, 3, 1.6)))))  vplot(race) |>   mark_bar(x = cat, y = value, fill = cat) |>   coord_flip() |>   transition_states(year, transition_length = 2, state_length = 1) |>   labs(title = "Bar chart race") |>   animate(nframes = 60, fps = 12) |>   (\(a) anim_save("race.gif", a))()

title: Effects and themes
text: theme sets look everything mark. vellumplot ships several. theme_gray() default (grey panel, white gridlines); theme_minimal() drops panel fill; theme_bw() white panel light grey gridlines; theme_classic() gives axis lines gridlines; theme_void() strips everything marks, legend, titles.
code: vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = factor(cyl)) |>   theme_minimal()

title: Effects and themes
text: theme() overrides individual slots, slot described typed element: element_text(), element_line(), element_rect(), element_blank() draw nothing. Slot names follow familiar dotted scheme (panel.grid.minor, axis.title, plot.title, ), property left NULL inherited parent theme tree. Long category names discrete axis perennial nuisance: side side collide. Two theme controls handle . Setting angle axis.text.x rotates tick labels, gutter reserves extra height automatically; explicit hjust/vjust sets anchor, otherwise end run pinned tick slant clears panel. Left horizontal, long label overrun width tick instead wraps onto multiple lines, label row grows fit — per-tick companion title/subtitle/caption wrapping. Labels already fit untouched, plain numeric axis unchanged.
code: vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   theme_bw() |>   theme(     panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),     plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),     axis.title = element_text(color = "grey30")   ) |>   labs(title = "Fuel economy") gdp <- data.frame(   country = c(     "United States", "United Kingdom", "United Arab Emirates",     "Republic of Korea", "Czech Republic"   ),   score = c(9, 6, 7, 8, 5) ) vplot(gdp) |>   mark_bar(x = country, y = score) |>   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45)) vplot(gdp) |>   mark_bar(x = country, y = score)

code: vplot(data.frame(x = 1, y = 1, lab = "NEON"), width = 5, height = 2.2) |>   mark_text(x = x, y = y, label = lab, size = 42, color = "#00e5ff",     effects = list(glow())) |>   theme_cyberpunk() vplot(pressure) |>   mark_line(     x = temperature, y = pressure,     effects = list(shadow(), outline(color = "white", size = 2))   ) vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, size = 4, effects = list(motion(x = 4))) vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = factor(cyl), effects = list(glow())) |>   theme_cyberpunk()

Independent shared scales mix freely: hp keeps one size legend panel rescales colours. per-panel legends sit right panel default; column panels gets legend track wide widest legend . follow theme(legend.position = ), "bottom" puts panel (one track per row panels, facet_grid() ) "inside" inside panel, legend.justification aligns along panel edge. collect legend area instead, give guide position. legend titled scale title panel’s strip text: guide position "panel" works shared scale : one legend repeated beside every panel. colours longer comparable panels, independent scale suits panels read one time. unfaceted plot single panel ignores setting.

code: p1 <- vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = factor(cyl)) p2 <- vplot(mtcars) |> mark_boxplot(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg) p3 <- vplot(mtcars) |> mark_histogram(x = mpg, bins = 10)  concat(p1, p2, p3, ncol = 3) concat(p1, p2, ncol = 1, heights = c(2, 1)) main <- vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) mini <- vplot(mtcars) |> mark_histogram(x = mpg, bins = 8) inset(main, mini, left = 0.6, bottom = 0.6, right = 0.98, top = 0.98) set.seed(1) vsparkline(cumsum(rnorm(40)), width = 60, height = 16) vsparkline(rpois(24, 6), type = "bar", color = "steelblue", width = 60, height = 16) spark <- vsparkline(cumsum(rnorm(40))) inset(main, spark, left = 0.62, bottom = 0.9, right = 0.98, top = 0.99) set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   metric = c("Revenue", "Users", "Latency", "Errors"),   latest = c(4213, 18402, 128, 37),   change = c("+4.2%", "+1.1%", "-8ms", "-12%") ) df$trend <- lapply(1:4, function(i) cumsum(rnorm(24))) df$volume <- lapply(1:4, function(i) rpois(20, 6))  vtable(df, spark = list(trend = "line", volume = "bar"), row_height = 8) set.seed(1) vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   annotate(     "sparkline",     x = 4, y = 33, values = cumsum(rnorm(30)),     width = 32, height = 10, halign = "left"   ) library(gt) #>  #> Attaching package: 'gt' #> The following object is masked from 'package:vellumplot': #>  #>     md set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(metric = c("Revenue", "Users", "Latency", "Errors")) df$trend <- lapply(1:4, function(i) cumsum(rnorm(24))) df$volume <- lapply(1:4, function(i) rpois(20, 6))  gt(df) |>   gt_vsparkline(trend, type = "line") |>   gt_vsparkline(volume, type = "bar", color = "#4682b4") plot_svg(   vsparkline(cumsum(rnorm(20)), color = "grey30"),   inline = TRUE, recolor = c(grey30 = "currentColor") )

title: Facets and composition
text: vtable() lays data frame grid cells: ordinary columns render text, list-column numeric vectors renders per-row sparkline. whole table one vector scene, prints exports like plot — chart--table without leaving plotting pipeline. Map column type ("line"/"bar"/"winloss") builder function full control, e.g. spark = list(trend = \(v) vsparkline(v, color = "steelblue")).
code: set.seed(1) df <- data.frame(   metric = c("Revenue", "Users", "Latency", "Errors"),   latest = c(4213, 18402, 128, 37),   change = c("+4.2%", "+1.1%", "-8ms", "-12%") ) df$trend <- lapply(1:4, function(i) cumsum(rnorm(24))) df$volume <- lapply(1:4, function(i) rpois(20, 6))  vtable(df, spark = list(trend = "line", volume = "bar"), row_height = 8)

title: Facets and composition
text: annotate("sparkline", …) drops sparkline data coordinate — little trend callout inside plot. generally, annotate("grob", grob = …) places vellum grob (PlotSpec) coordinate, sized physical units anchored halign/valign.
code: set.seed(1) vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   annotate(     "sparkline",     x = 4, y = 33, values = cumsum(rnorm(30)),     width = 32, height = 10, halign = "left"   )

title: Facets and composition
text: render_plot() writes one figure one file. Two companions handle many figures . pdf_pages() writes list plots single PDF, one plot per page — report slide deck. Pages may differ size (plot keeps width/height), per-page accessibility tags (see Accessibility) written every page. Given single faceted plot instead list, pdf_pages() splits one page per facet cell — paged counterpart small-multiple grid, page trains scales tagged independently: render_all() goes way: list plots separate files, rendered across CPU cores. plot one independent job, work parallelises cleanly (via process forks macOS/Linux, sequentially Windows) output byte-identical rendering one one. list named, paths may single directory plot lands <name>.png:
code: report <- list(   vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |> labs(title = "Weight vs mpg"),   vplot(mtcars) |> mark_histogram(x = mpg, bins = 10) |> labs(title = "mpg") ) pdf_pages(report, "report.pdf") vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   facet_wrap(~cyl) |>   pdf_pages("by-cylinder.pdf") render_all(   list(     weight = vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg),     power = vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = hp, y = mpg)   ),   "figures/" )

title: Flows and hierarchies
text: vsankey() draws layered flow diagram flow list: one row per flow, node, node, value sets ribbon’s width. Nodes union values; node appears target source (, Grid) makes diagram multi-stage. Columns placed longest-path layering flows, nodes within column ordered minimise ribbon crossings (deterministic barycenter sweep). node’s height proportional larger total - -flow, ribbon widths proportional value — diagram reads conserved flow left right. Ribbons coloured source node default; flow_color = "target" colours target instead, flow_color = "gradient" fades ribbon source colour target colour. show_values = TRUE appends node’s value label, node_width / node_gap tune node rectangles. flows must form directed acyclic graph (node reach ), values must positive. Turn node labels label = FALSE: vsankey() returns ordinary [PlotSpec], renders render_plot() / print() like plot. hood adds single mark_sankey() layer axis-free, free-aspect panel; mark_sankey() exported , building flow layer plot set .

title: Declarative interactivity
text: bind_scale() binds view’s scale domain interval selection defined another view. Brush small overview detail zooms brushed range; clear brush (click empty space, Escape) detail zooms back . Vega-Lite’s overview + detail, detail’s scale.domain names brush: detail keeps scales; host changes part visible re-ticks axes range (display-tier zoom, nothing recomputed). Bind several views one brush, bind "x" "y" rectangular brush. view brush drawn never zooms . Shiny, every panel’s visible range arrives input$<id>_zoom$panels, keyed panel name; composition names panels per cell ("cell-1-panel-1-1" detail , "cell-2-panel-1-1" overview). select_interval(bind = "scales") Vega-Lite’s half: brush drawn. selection view’s pan/zoom domain, zooming panning view (wheel, pinch, navigator, drag pan mode, becomes default drag) writes interval, resetting zoom empties . bind_scale() another view follows (linked zoom), condition() / filter_by() react whatever view:

what: What a host does with it
title: Declarative interactivity
text: vellumplot compiles carries interaction declarations plus per-element metadata host needs (interaction_model() returns declaration block). host reads wires gestures already performs frozen scene — highlight, hide, pan/zoom — recompilation. Turn plots live widget : interaction display-tier design: reacts frozen scene (highlight, filter--hiding, pan/zoom) never recomputes grammar. See select_point(), select_interval(), condition(), filter_by(), add_selection(), bind_scale() reference.
code: library(vellumwidget) vplot(df) |>   mark_point(x = x, y = y, color = condition("hi", cyl, "grey80")) |>   select_point("hi", on = "hover") |>   as_widget()

title: Marks, layer by layer
text: mark_point() draws markers; mark_line() mark_step() connect points x order; mark_rule() draws reference lines. mark_point() also takes shape (one "circle", "square", "triangle", "diamond", "plus", "cross") position = "jitter" adjustment. shape also accepts SVG icon — path d string (icon sets ship) .svg file — drawn crisp vector marker. Use literal string constant icon, map shape give [scale_shape()] one icon per level (legend shows icons); size scales . mark_bar() draws bars zero baseline. Give explicit y heights, omit y counts rows per category (count stat). fill mapped, groups stack default; switch side--side position = "dodge" normalise 1 position = "fill". finer control, position argument also takes parameterised position_*() object. position_dodge2() fills category’s band groups actually present (ragged grouping stays centred); position_nudge() offsets constant; position_jitter(width=, seed=) position_jitterdodge() control scatter overplotted categorical points.
code: vplot(pressure) |>   mark_line(x = temperature, y = pressure) |>   mark_point(x = temperature, y = pressure) star <- "M12 2l3 7h7l-5.5 4.5 2 7-6.5-4.5-6.5 4.5 2-7L2 9h7z" heart <- "M12 21s-7-4.35-9.5-8.5C1 9 2.5 5 6 5c2 0 3.5 1.5 4 2.5C10.5 6.5 12 5 14 5c3.5 0 5 4 3.5 7.5C19 16.65 12 21 12 21z" d <- data.frame(x = 1:6, y = c(2, 4, 3, 5, 4, 6), g = rep(c("a", "b"), 3)) vplot(d) |>   mark_point(x = x, y = y, shape = g, color = g, size = 1.6) |>   scale_shape(values = c(a = heart, b = star)) vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_bar(x = factor(cyl), fill = factor(gear), position = "dodge") vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_bar(x = factor(cyl), fill = factor(gear), position = position_dodge2(padding = 0.15))

title: Marks, layer by layer
text: mark_area() fills y line zero, mark_ribbon() fills ymin ymax, interval marks draw ranges: mark_errorbar() (caps), mark_linerange() (without), mark_segment() (x, y) (xend, yend). mark_boxplot() summarises raw y values per x category box--whisker (box Q1 Q3, median line, whiskers 1.5 times IQR, outliers points). Like points bars, summary marks addressable: error bar line range keyed data_id/tooltip carries identity every segment draws, boxplot keys box category — hover, tooltip, select units rendered interactive widget. mark_pointrange() mark_crossbar() identity summary marks: supply y, ymin, ymax (e.g. model’s estimate interval) draw point--range box--centre-line — aggregation.
code: vplot(pressure) |>   mark_area(x = temperature, y = pressure, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.4) |>   mark_line(x = temperature, y = pressure) vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_boxplot(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg)

title: Marks, layer by layer
text: mark_abline() draws sloped reference line y = slope * x + intercept, diagonal companion mark_rule()’s horizontal vertical lines. slope intercept may vectors draw family lines. mark_function() draws curve y = fun(x) sampled across panel’s x range — handy eyeballing theoretical distribution data. Overlay normal density density histogram: reuse panel’s existing scales, add top data layer. (mark_function() holds live function, round-trip as_spec().) many observations land (x, y) — common rounded discrete data — mark_count() collapses one bubble sized overlap count, honest alternative invisible overplotting:
code: vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   mark_abline(slope = -5, intercept = 37, color = "firebrick") set.seed(1) vplot(data.frame(z = rnorm(500))) |>   mark_histogram(x = z, y = after_stat(density)) |>   mark_function(fun = dnorm, color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5) vplot(data.frame(cyl = mtcars$cyl, gear = mtcars$gear)) |>   mark_count(x = cyl, y = gear)

See statistical marks article details.

title: Marks, layer by layer
text: mark_text() draws label aesthetic text (x, y); mark_label() adds filled background behind label stays legible busy marks. size points, angle can mapped constant. crowded scatter, labels collide. repel = TRUE moves apart draws thin leader back point. Placement solved engine device pixels applied absolute offset, drift data scale deterministic (seed needed). offset coordinate agnostic, repel also works faceted polar plots — panel solved labels kept inside . mark_text_path() sets label along curve instead point – one label per group, glyphs following group’s path rotated local tangent. direct way label line without legend, caption contour arc. Glyphs follow tangent, path walked right--left reads upside-– traverse reading direction (sin rising half-period). mark_series_label() legend-free way name lines: puts series’ name end (point largest x), coloured match repelled apart. Map x/y/color lines — label text colour follow series. Give panel little x-room drop now-redundant colour legend. mark_outlier_label() labels points stand — keeps rows whose y outlier (Tukey’s IQR rule, method = "sd") labels just , busy scatter names extremes without wall text. Map label name outlier; color/fill mapped, outliers found within group.
code: top <- mtcars[mtcars$mpg > 30, ] vplot(top) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   mark_text(x = wt, y = mpg, label = rownames(top), vjust = "bottom", size = 9) vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   mark_text(     x = wt, y = mpg, label = rownames(mtcars),     repel = TRUE, size = 4   ) t <- seq(0, pi, length.out = 60) curve <- data.frame(x = t, y = sin(t), lab = "y = sin(x)") vplot(curve) |>   mark_text_path(x = x, y = y, label = lab, size = 9, vjust = "bottom", offset = 2) set.seed(1) econ <- data.frame(   year = rep(2000:2015, 3),   value = c(     cumsum(rnorm(16, 2)), cumsum(rnorm(16, 1)), cumsum(rnorm(16, 3))   ),   series = rep(c("north", "south", "east"), each = 16) ) vplot(econ) |>   mark_line(x = year, y = value, color = series) |>   mark_series_label(x = year, y = value, color = series) |>   xlim(2000, 2018) |>   guides(color = "none") vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   mark_outlier_label(x = wt, y = mpg, label = rownames(mtcars))

text: mark_image() puts bitmap (x, y) place marker: flag company logo. src column file paths (one image per datum) single path reused every point. size sets height millimetres, width follows image’s aspect ratio, nothing stretches. Reading images needs magick package (suggested dependency), decodes PNG, JPEG, SVG, . size millimetres rather data units, images keep physical size panel resizes.
code: badge <- function(text, fill) {   path <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")   magick::image_blank(120, 120, color = fill) |>     magick::image_annotate(text, size = 64, gravity = "center", color = "white") |>     magick::image_write(path)   path } d <- data.frame(   x = 1:3,   y = c(2, 3, 1),   logo = c(badge("A", "tomato"), badge("B", "steelblue"), badge("C", "seagreen")) ) vplot(d) |>   mark_image(x = x, y = y, src = logo, size = 14)

title: Scales and guides
text: Continuous data get smooth colour ramp; discrete data get categorical palette. palette argument takes vector colours single palette name passed grDevices::hcl.colors() (example "Batlow", "Blues", "Set 2"). two-colour ramp, scale_color_gradient() takes endpoints directly, scale_color_gradientn() arbitrary n-stop ramp. coming ggplot2, familiar named constructors simply wrappers palette =: scale_color_viridis_c() / _d() viridis maps, scale_color_brewer() (discrete) / scale_color_distiller() (continuous) ColorBrewer-style palettes. Set limits = continuous colour scale fix mapped range. categories, scale_color_manual() maps levels colours; naming values pins level specific colour. signed anomaly data — value like zero meaningfully neutral — scale_color_gradient2() (scale_fill_gradient2()) draw diverging ramp around midpoint. rescales midpoint, neutral mid colour always lands value even data range lopsided: Ramps built plain colour vector — scale_color_gradient(low, high), palette given colours — interpolated perceptually-uniform Oklab space, sRGB, ramp colourbar read evenly instead dipping muddy, -dark middle (blue→yellow ramp longer passes grey). Designed perceptual palettes default Batlow hcl.colors() name already uniform unchanged. blend sRGB (CIE Lab) instead, set options(vellumplot.color.interpolation = "srgb") ("lab"). gradient fill opts per gradient linear_gradient(..., interpolation = "oklab").

Categorical axes use scale_x_discrete() scale_y_discrete(), whose limits set order subset levels. "log10" go — data crosses zero spans positive negative values several orders magnitude — "symlog" gives symmetric-log axis: linear zero, logarithmic tail, ticks zero signed powers ten. set limits without spelling whole scale, use shortcuts xlim(), ylim(), lims() (last takes one named argument per aesthetic): scale_*(trans=) () transforms data: picks breaks transformed space, "log10" axis labelled 1, 10, 100. coord_trans() instead warps display, scale trained — breaks stay original data values, axis keeps labels sit warped positions (gridlines bunch , straight lines curve). Use show data log display without relabelling axis powers ten: x / y takes transform name ("log10", "sqrt", "identity") scales::transform_*() object. applies common marks (points, lines, areas, bars, tiles, smooths, text); interval/segment, boxplot, raster marks warped yet. secondary axis adds second set ticks labels opposite edge (top x, right y), computed 1:1 monotonic transform primary axis. Pass sec_axis() sec.axis argument continuous position scale. classic use unit conversion — plot Celsius, label top Fahrenheit: dup_axis() identity special case — simply duplicates axis far edge, handy reading wide plot either side: transform can formula (~ . * 2), function, scales::transform_*() object, must monotonic. labelling convenience, independent second axis data. currently supported continuous position scales default Cartesian coordinate system, shared scales across facets; combining coord_flip() / coord_polar() / coord_trans(), free facet scales, add_marginal() raises error, plot composition secondary axis drawn.

title: Scales and guides
text: guides() overrides single legend without respelling scale. Pass "none" hide , guide_legend() reverse key order override title. Hiding legend keeps mapping; marks stay coloured, guide disappears: Every legend guide takes position = ("right", "left", "top", "bottom" "inside"), overrides theme(legend.position = ) one legend, ggplot2 3.5. Legends can sit different sides one plot; legend top bottom laid horizontally. override.aes styles legend keys independently data — fix scatter small, translucent points whose keys still want big readable. Pass named list aesthetics (size, alpha, colour, fill, shape, linewidth); swatches change, never marks. continuous colour scale guide colour bar. guide_colourbar() sizes (barwidth / barheight, mm), toggles break ticks (colour), moves labels left bar. binned colour scale draws discrete swatches default; guide_coloursteps() renders segmented bar instead, labelled bin boundaries (takes barwidth / barheight / ticks tunables). size legend defaults stacked keys; guide_legend(nested = TRUE) draws proportional-symbol legend — concentric circles sharing baseline, leader label. reads size directly compact, suits wide size range circles large enough tell apart.

code: vgraph(g, layout = "stress") |>   mark_edges(alpha = 0.3) |>   mark_nodes(size = deg, fill = grp) |>   mark_node_text(label = name, top_n = 8, by = deg) |>   select_neighbours(on = "hover") |>   scale_size(range = c(0.5, 3))

Stochastic layouts take seed figure reproducible. still ordinary specs. face scales, themes, composition tools plot, render file render_plot(). per-feature interactivity (tooltips data keys map features nodes), see interactivity notes mark_sf() mark reference pages.
code: vgraph(g, layout = "circle") |>   mark_edges(alpha = 0.3) |>   mark_nodes(fill = grp, size = 2)

title: Specs, agents, and interoperability
text: as_spec() turns plot nested list; from_spec() rebuilds . JSON form wire format. serializer covers encoding-level grammar exactly. Anything portable document carry — custom transform functions, paint/pattern fills, hand-drawn sketch() geometry, secondary axes, sf CRS objects, per-layer data — refused classed vellumplot_unserializable error naming slot, never silently dropped. (Theme one exception: preset name scalar settings round-trip; custom element overrides drop warning, since styling orthogonal data spec.) Data inlined small stored reference (content hash + column schema) otherwise.
code: p <- vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = factor(cyl)) |>   labs(title = "Fuel economy")  spec <- as_spec(p) str(spec$layers[[1]], max.level = 2) #> List of 3 #>  $ mark       : chr "point" #>  $ encoding   :List of 3 #>   ..$ x    :List of 1 #>   ..$ y    :List of 1 #>   ..$ color:List of 1 #>  $ stat_params:List of 1 #>   ..$ auto: logi FALSE  json <- spec_to_json(p) identical(as_spec(spec_from_json(json))$layers, as_spec(p)$layers) #> [1] TRUE

title: Specs, agents, and interoperability
text: serializable spec makes vellumplot safe target LLM / agent generation: agent emits data (spec) validate render trusted code — never eval()-d R. Three pieces support loop. spec_fields() grounds model real columns inferred types: vplot_from_spec() validates generated spec data returns structured diagnostics — machine-readable repair loop — instead traceback: mcp_serve() runs pure-R Model Context Protocol server exposing get_schema, list_fields, render_spec tools. Point agent bundled launcher: vplot_ask() model-agnostic convenience: give responder function (wrapping model MCP client) assembles grounding payload validates result.
code: spec_fields(mtcars) #>    name         type   class n_unique            examples #> 1   mpg quantitative numeric       25    21.0, 22.8, 21.4 #> 2   cyl quantitative numeric        3             6, 4, 8 #> 3  disp quantitative numeric       27       160, 108, 258 #> 4    hp quantitative numeric       22        110, 93, 175 #> 5  drat quantitative numeric       22    3.90, 3.85, 3.08 #> 6    wt quantitative numeric       29 2.620, 2.875, 2.320 #> 7  qsec quantitative numeric       30 16.46, 17.02, 18.61 #> 8    vs quantitative numeric        2                0, 1 #> 9    am quantitative numeric        2                1, 0 #> 10 gear quantitative numeric        3             4, 3, 5 #> 11 carb quantitative numeric        6             4, 1, 2 bad <- spec bad$layers[[1]]$encoding$x$field <- "weight" # a hallucinated column d <- spec_diagnose(bad, data = mtcars) d$ok #> [1] FALSE d$diagnostics[[1]] #> $severity #> [1] "error" #>  #> $field #> [1] "weight" #>  #> $message #> [1] "Unknown field 'weight'." #>  #> $hint #> [1] "Available fields: mpg, cyl, disp, hp, drat, wt, qsec, vs, am, gear, carb." Rscript -e 'vellumplot::mcp_serve()'

what: Provenance: tracing a plot back to its data
title: Specs, agents, and interoperability
text: Every drawn element keeps stable id tying data rows produced . provenance_join() surfaces alongside element’s device-pixel geometry: figure can also carry fingerprint data, verifies data drawn : provenance_payload() exposes element → rows mapping payload host (vellumwidget) can use click--source interaction.
code: pj <- provenance_join(p) pj[, c("id", "mark", "n_rows")] #>                 id  mark n_rows #> 1 layer-1-point-g1 point      7 #> 2 layer-1-point-g2 point     11 #> 3 layer-1-point-g3 point     14 pj$rows[[1]] # the source-data rows behind the first element #> [1]  1  2  4  6 10 11 30 svg <- plot_svg(p, manifest = TRUE) plot_verify(svg, mtcars)$ok # TRUE #> [1] TRUE plot_verify(svg, mtcars[1:5, ])$ok # FALSE — different data #> [1] FALSE

title: Statistical marks
text: mark_histogram() bins continuous x draws per-bin counts bars. Control resolution bins. mark_density() draws smooth kernel-density estimate x filled curve; adjust scales bandwidth. Densities comparable vertical scale, mapping fill group overlaying works well.
code: vplot(faithful) |>   mark_histogram(x = waiting, bins = 25) vplot(penguins) |>   mark_density(x = bill_len, fill = species, alpha = 0.4) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing non-finite values (`mark_density()`).

title: Statistical marks
text: scatter shows joint distribution two variables hides one . add_marginal() puts back: draws distribution x along top edge y along right edge, scale panel lines points. vellumplot counterpart ggExtra::ggMarginal(). Unlike marks article, add_marginal() plot modifier rather layer, closer facet_wrap() mark_density(). takes encoding ; reads x y first plain layer (mark_point()) computes margins . type = "histogram" bins values instead smoothing , sides picks edges draw. scatter maps discrete color fill, group = TRUE splits margin way, per-group density sits points matching colour. scatter’s legend already names groups, none added. Margins share panel’s scales reserve space around single panel, version combine facets, flipped polar coordinate system, fixed aspect ratio.
code: vplot(faithful) |>   mark_point(x = eruptions, y = waiting) |>   add_marginal() vplot(faithful) |>   mark_point(x = eruptions, y = waiting) |>   add_marginal(type = "histogram", sides = "t", bins = 20) vplot(penguins) |>   mark_point(x = bill_len, y = bill_dep, color = species) |>   add_marginal(group = TRUE) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values (layer 1, `mark_point()`).

title: Statistical marks
text: mark_summary() aggregates y within x category using fun (mean default) draws result. quick way add group means raw data.
code: vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg, color = "grey60") |>   mark_summary(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg, fun = median)

title: Statistical marks
text: mark_signif() runs pairwise test x groups draws bracket p-value comparison — ggsignif / ggpubr idiom. Add top boxplot violin; brackets stack data y-axis grows fit. comparisons list group pairs test (default: adjacent pair); method "wilcox.test" "t.test"; label p-value stars.
code: set.seed(1) d <- data.frame(   grp = rep(c("ctrl", "low", "high"), each = 40),   y = c(rnorm(40), rnorm(40, 0.4), rnorm(40, 1.2)) ) vplot(d) |>   mark_boxplot(x = grp, y = y, fill = grp) |>   mark_signif(     x = grp, y = y,     comparisons = list(c("ctrl", "low"), c("ctrl", "high")),     label = "stars"   )

title: Statistical marks
text: mark_smooth() fits model y x (per group) draws fitted line confidence ribbon se = TRUE. layers naturally raw points. method chooses fit: "lm" (linear), "loess" (local regression, span controlling neighbourhood), "glm" (family via method.args, e.g. logistic), "gam" (penalised smooth, needs ), "rq" (quantile regression, needs ). default "auto" picks loess small groups gam large ones.
code: vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   mark_smooth(x = wt, y = mpg, se = TRUE, level = 0.95) vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   mark_smooth(x = wt, y = mpg, method = "loess", span = 0.9)

title: Statistical marks
text: mark_ellipse() mark_hull() enclose set points single region — way read group separation scatter without drawing every point’s membership. color fill mapped, group gets region. mark_ellipse() draws covariance ellipse (robust t distribution default, "norm" / "euclid"), following ggplot2’s stat_ellipse(): mark_hull() draws convex hull instead. unfilled boundaries default (matching ggplot2); map set fill shade :
code: vplot(iris) |>   mark_point(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, color = Species) |>   mark_ellipse(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, color = Species) vplot(iris) |>   mark_point(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, color = Species) |>   mark_hull(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species, alpha = 0.2)

title: Statistical marks
text: mark_line(window = ) transforms line’s y drawing — rolling statistic, running total, lag/lead — computed per group rows ordered x. Pass op name list(op, k, ...). 7-point trailing mean rides raw series: ops cover rolling mean/sum/median/min/max (k, align, partial), running cumsum/cummean/cummax/cummin, lag/lead, rank.
code: set.seed(1) ts <- data.frame(day = 1:120, value = cumsum(rnorm(120))) vplot(ts) |>   mark_line(x = day, y = value, color = "grey70") |>   mark_line(x = day, y = value, window = list(op = "mean", k = 7))

title: Statistical marks
text: Several marks summarise single variable distributed. mark_ecdf() draws empirical cumulative distribution x step, scale-free way compare groups without choosing bandwidth. mark_qq() plots sorted sample quantiles reference distribution (normal default); mark_qq_line() adds reference line quartiles. Points line mean sample matches reference. mark_rug() adds marginal ticks observation, compact companion scatter density. sides picks edges ("b", "l", "t", "r").
code: vplot(penguins) |>   mark_ecdf(x = bill_len, color = species) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing non-finite values (`mark_ecdf()`). vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_qq(sample = mpg) |>   mark_qq_line(sample = mpg) vplot(faithful) |>   mark_point(x = waiting, y = eruptions) |>   mark_rug()

title: Statistical marks
text: mark_violin() draws mirrored kernel density y categorical x, boxplot’s silhouette shows full shape group. mark_ridgeline() turns side: density x per categorical y, ridges overlapping many groups fit little vertical space. Use height argument tune much overlap. mark_dotplot() bins x stacks one dot per observation, height stack count can read dot dot.
code: vplot(penguins) |>   mark_violin(x = species, y = bill_len, fill = species) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values (layer 1, `mark_violin()`). vplot(penguins) |>   mark_ridgeline(x = bill_len, y = species, fill = species) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values (layer 1, #> `mark_ridgeline()`). vplot(faithful) |>   mark_dotplot(x = waiting)

title: Statistical marks
text: x category many draws — posterior samples, bootstrap — -style marks show distribution’s shape summary intervals together. mark_halfeye() draws one-sided density slab point-interval base (median, thick inner interval, thin outer one); mark_interval() point-interval alone. Set interval probabilities .width.
code: set.seed(1) draws <- data.frame(   model = rep(c("prior", "posterior", "pooled"), each = 800),   estimate = rnorm(2400, rep(c(0, 1.5, 1), each = 800), rep(c(1, 0.5, 0.7), each = 800)) ) vplot(draws) |>   mark_halfeye(x = model, y = estimate, .width = c(0.66, 0.95))

title: Statistical marks
text: raincloud pairs density “cloud” raw observations “rain” — shape every data point . mark_raincloud() composes one call (mark_halfeye() plus mark_point() sina spread), color/fill flows : rain uses position_sina(), spreads group’s points along x proportion local density — point cloud echoes violin’s shape rather flat jitter. Reach directly plain scatter categorical x want see every observation:
code: vplot(penguins) |>   mark_raincloud(x = species, y = bill_len, color = species) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values (layer 1, `mark_halfeye()`). #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values (layer 2, `mark_point()`). vplot(penguins) |>   mark_point(x = species, y = bill_len, color = species, position = "sina") #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values (layer 1, `mark_point()`).

title: Statistical marks
text: mark_contour() estimates 2-D density point cloud draws iso-density contour lines; mark_contour_filled() fills bands . coloured level automatically. read best points summarise: density estimate uses MASS::kde2d(); tune levels bins, binwidth, explicit breaks. contour surface already (z value regular x/y grid) rather point density, map z: Contour tracing done engine (vellum::vl_contour()), needs extra package; density field additionally uses MASS estimate.
code: vplot(faithful) |>   mark_point(x = eruptions, y = waiting, color = "grey70") |>   mark_contour(x = eruptions, y = waiting) vplot(faithful) |>   mark_contour_filled(x = eruptions, y = waiting) grid <- expand.grid(x = seq(-3, 3, 0.1), y = seq(-3, 3, 0.1)) grid$z <- with(grid, dnorm(x) * dnorm(y)) vplot(grid) |> mark_contour(x = x, y = y, z = z)

Map discrete color (fill) aesthetic shade categorically (datashader’s count_cat): category aggregated separately every cell coloured count-weighted mix categories holds, opacity density — colour legend. mark_point() also auto = TRUE switch falls back datashaded raster automatically layer many rows, can keep writing mark_point() let vellumplot choose representation.

title: A grammar of graphics on the vellum backend
text: Building plot returns spec; printing draws Plots pane (embeds knitr/Quarto chunk), like ggplot2. Use render_plot() write file. Layer marks single panel; scales train across every layer: Facet grid panels (facet_wrap() / facet_grid()), shared free scales: Draw spatial data: mark_sf() renders sf geometry column coord_sf() reprojects locks map aspect ratio: Draw network: vgraph() lays igraph graph (stress majorization default), mark_edges() / mark_nodes() draw , aspect-locked without axes, edges nodes: spec just data, summary() shows structure without drawing: Write file render_plot() (format follows extension):
code: library(vellumplot)  # a scatter with a continuous colour legend vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp) |>   scale_color_continuous() vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   mark_smooth(x = wt, y = mpg) vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   facet_wrap(~cyl) nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"), quiet = TRUE) vplot(nc) |>   mark_sf(fill = BIR74) |>   coord_sf() g <- igraph::make_graph("Zachary") g <- igraph::set_vertex_attr(   g,   "grp",   value = as.factor(igraph::cluster_louvain(g)$membership) ) g <- igraph::set_vertex_attr(g, "deg", value = igraph::degree(g)) vgraph(g, layout = "stress") |>   mark_edges(alpha = 0.4) |>   mark_nodes(size = deg, fill = grp) |>   scale_size(range = c(2, 8)) summary(vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp)) #> <PlotSpec> 32x11 (11 columns), page 6x4 in #>  #> ── layers #> • mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg, color = hp) p <- vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) render_plot(p, "cars.png")

title: A grammar of graphics on the vellum backend
text: Marks: mark_point(), mark_line(), mark_step(), mark_rule(), mark_bar() (explicit heights, row counts per category), mark_area() / mark_ribbon(), intervals (mark_errorbar(), mark_linerange(), mark_segment()), mark_boxplot(), tiles/heatmaps (mark_tile(), mark_raster()), 2-D binning (mark_bin2d(), mark_hex()), 2-D density contours (mark_contour(), mark_contour_filled()), text (mark_text(), mark_label()), pie/donut shortcuts (mark_pie(), mark_donut()). Spatial: mark_sf() draws sf geometry column map layer, coord_sf() reproject lock aspect ratio. Network: vgraph() starts node-link diagram igraph graph (stress layout default, via graphlayouts), mark_edges(), mark_nodes(), mark_node_text(), scale_edge_width(). Encodings (tidy-eval): x, y, color/fill, size, shape, alpha. Position scales (scale_x_continuous(), scale_y_continuous(); linear log10) auto-trained, expanded domains; discrete band scales (scale_x_discrete(), scale_y_discrete()) categorical axes. Colour scales (scale_color_continuous() / scale_fill_continuous(), scale_color_discrete() / scale_fill_discrete(), _gradient(), _binned(), _manual()), scale_shape(), trained scale_size() / scale_linewidth(), stacked legends. Trained axes, panel gridlines, layering one panel. Faceting (facet_wrap(), facet_grid()) shared free scales, via resolve_scale() lattice. Statistical marks: mark_histogram(), mark_density(), mark_summary(), mark_smooth() (after_stat()). Coordinate systems: coord_cartesian(), coord_flip(), coord_fixed() / coord_equal(), coord_trans() (nonlinear display remap), coord_polar() (pie / coxcomb / radar), coord_sf(). Position adjustments: stack / dodge / fill bars, jittered points. Per-mark blend = modes (CSS mix-blend-mode: "multiply", "screen", …). mark_datashade() million-point density rasters. Annotations: annotate(), labs(), md() markdown titles. Themes (theme_gray() default, theme_minimal(), theme_bw(), theme_classic(), theme_void(), theme_cyberpunk(), theme() / set_theme()) multi-plot composition (hconcat(), vconcat(), concat(), wrap_plots(), inset(), repeat_()). Layer effects (glow(), outline(), shadow(), motion(), echo()) gradient fills (linear_gradient(), radial_gradient()). Pattern (hatch) fills: pattern_stripe(), pattern_crosshatch(), pattern_grid(), pattern_dot(), pattern_checker(), mapped via scale_pattern(), greyscale- colour-vision-safe, every backend. Boolean marks: vvenn() draws 2-/3-set Venn/Euler diagrams solid geometry, mark_sf(merge = TRUE) dissolves adjacent -value regions one. Intervals equal-tailed quantile intervals .width probabilities (widest drawn thinnest). Supply many draws per x (e.g. posterior samples).

title: Uncertainty marks (slab + interval) — mark_halfeye
code: set.seed(1) draws <- data.frame(   grp = rep(c("a", "b", "c"), each = 400),   val = rnorm(1200, rep(c(0, 1, 2), each = 400)) ) vplot(draws) |> mark_halfeye(x = grp, y = val)  vplot(draws) |> mark_interval(x = grp, y = val)  # horizontal: the discrete variable on y vplot(draws) |> mark_halfeye(x = val, y = grp)

title: Statistical marks — mark_histogram
text: Marks apply statistical transform drawing. mark_histogram() bins continuous x draws per-bin counts bars. bin stat computes count, density (group integrates 1), ncount ndensity (scaled maximum 1), width, after_stat(). mark_smooth() fits model y x (per group) draws fitted line, confidence ribbon se = TRUE.

title: Statistical marks — mark_histogram
text: plot PlotSpec (vplot()). ... Encodings (tidy-eval), e.g. x, y, color/fill. bins Number histogram bins (default 30), used neither binwidth breaks given. ggplot2, outer bins centred smallest largest values unless boundary center set. binwidth Width bin, overriding bins. breaks numeric vector bin edges, overriding bins binwidth. Bins may different widths; values outside edges counted. boundary, center bins aligned: boundary position falls edge two bins, center one falls bin's centre (give one). Either may lie outside data. example binwidth = 1, boundary = 0 makes bins (0, 1], (1, 2], .... neither, bins given binwidth aligned binwidth / 2. closed side bin closed: "right" (default, (, b]) "left" ([, b)). outermost edges always count. position Position adjustment histogram bars ("stack", "dodge", "fill"). blend Optional blend mode compositing layer already drawn beneath (panel earlier layers), one CSS mix-blend-mode names, e.g. "multiply", "screen", "darken". whole layer composites one isolated group (per element). sketch sketch() spec giving layer hand-drawn look (wobbly outlines, hachure fills), NA/FALSE force crisp (overriding plot-wide theme_sketch()), NULL (default) inherit. Geometry marks accept ; text, raster, hex datashade marks . data Optional layer data frame; overrides plot data layer. method Smoothing method: one "auto", "lm", "loess", "glm", "gam", "rq". formula Model formula terms x y (e.g. y ~ poly(x, 2), y ~ s(x) gam). Defaults y ~ x (y ~ s(x) gam). span loess neighbourhood size (larger = smoother). se Draw confidence ribbon around smooth? Ignored "rq". level Confidence level ribbon. method.args Extra arguments fitting function, e.g. list(family = binomial()) glm, list(tau = 0.9) rq.

title: Statistical marks — mark_histogram
text: mark_smooth() supports several methods: "auto" (default) picks "loess" small groups (< 1000 points) "gam" large ones. "lm" / "glm" — linear generalised linear fits (glm takes family via method.args, e.g. binomial() logistic). "loess" — local regression, controlled span. "gam" — generalised additive model smooth term (default y ~ s(x)); needs mgcv package. "rq" — quantile regression single method.args$tau (default median); needs quantreg package draws fitted line (confidence ribbon). several quantiles, add one layer per tau. mark_freqpoly() draws bin counts line bin centres (frequency polygon), one line per group. Like ggplot2's geom_freqpoly() adds empty bin end, line starts ends zero. takes binning arguments mark_histogram(), y = after_stat(density) draws densities instead counts.

title: Statistical marks — mark_histogram
code: vplot(mtcars) |> mark_histogram(x = mpg, bins = 10)  # bins of width 2 with an edge at 10: (10, 12], (12, 14], ... vplot(mtcars) |> mark_histogram(x = mpg, binwidth = 2, boundary = 10)  vplot(mtcars) |> mark_freqpoly(x = mpg, color = factor(cyl), binwidth = 2)  vplot(mtcars) |> mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |> mark_smooth(x = wt, y = mpg)  # local regression with a wider neighbourhood vplot(mtcars) |>   mark_point(x = wt, y = mpg) |>   mark_smooth(x = wt, y = mpg, method = "loess", span = 0.9)

text: render_all() renders list independent plots separate files across CPU cores — small multiples, batch export, one file per group. work embarrassingly parallel (one whole plot per worker), result byte-identical rendering one one. Parallelism uses process forks, speeds things macOS/Linux falls back sequential Windows; worth several substantial plots.

Passed vellum::render() (e.g. text, cvd).
